title: A job time that must exist

blocks.text: A batch scheduler reads each job's start as a local date and time in a zone. Twice a year that local time may be special:

items: In the spring **gap** the clocks skip an hour: in `America/New_York`, 2024-03-10 goes from 01:59 straight to 03:00, so 02:30 never happens.
In the autumn **overlap** they repeat one: on 2024-11-03, 01:00 to 01:59 happens first at `-04:00`, then again at `-05:00`.

blocks.text: Write `WallClock.at(LocalDateTime local, ZoneId zone)`, the job's start as a `ZonedDateTime`, under the scheduler's rules:

items: a time the clocks skip is **refused** with `IllegalArgumentException`, so the operator picks a real time; it is not quietly moved;
a time the clocks repeat is taken at its **second** occurrence, after the clocks went back.

cases.says: An ordinary local time gets the zone's only offset for that moment.
02:30 on the spring-forward day in New York, and 01:30 on London's, are refused.
01:30 on the fall-back day is taken after the clocks went back: -05:00 in New York, +00:00 in London.

concepts: A local time in a spring-forward gap does not exist, and ZonedDateTime.of silently moves it forward past the gap.
A local time in a fall-back overlap happens twice; ZonedDateTime takes the earlier offset unless withLaterOffsetAtOverlap picks the second.
